dial.summary: BOJ held at 1% (8-1 vote, Takata dissenting for a hike) on July 31 as expected, while Japan's FX intervention briefly drove DXY to 99.87—the first sub-100 print since June 17—before a partial recovery; BTC Accumulation thesis intact: BTC.D firm at 56.6%, BTC at $64,256, TOTAL at $2.27T, stablecoin dominance compressed to 13.4%, and near-zero perp funding (+0.004%/8h); real yields (2.41%) remain the primary headwind, but soft Q2 GDP (1.5%) and core PCE (0.1% MoM) are building the September rate pause narrative.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: MacroMicro 4-bank aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) June 2026 data remains the latest confirmed read at $102.7T; July 2026 data not yet published across all four central banks; component trajectory confirmed expanding: US M2 $22.67T (monthly gain ~1%), China M2 $49.96T (monthly gain ~2.73%), Europe M2 ~$19.4T (monthly gain ~2.71%)—all four central banks recording monthly gains per July 2026 data; 4-week trend up (June > May, YoY expansion intact across components); status supportive (4-week uptrend met; YoY contracting headwind condition not met).

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: June 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI confirmed at 53.3% (released July 1)—sixth consecutive expansion month, down 0.7pp from May's 54.0%; July 2026 ISM print releases August 3 at 10:00 AM ET; S&P Global US Manufacturing flash PMI for July edged down to 53.8 from 53.9, offering a cautious advance signal; June sub-indicators: new orders 56.0%, prices paid 73.0%, employment 49.7%; 4-week trend down (54.0% May → 53.3% June, -0.7pp, above the 0.5pp relative threshold); status neutral (above 50 but falling—supportive requires above 50 AND rising).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY traded to an intraday low of 99.87 on July 31, 2026—lowest since June 17—following Japan's FX intervention (USD/JPY briefly plunged from ~162.80 to ~157.00 in the Asia session) combined with lingering softness from Q2 GDP miss (1.5% vs 2.1% est) and soft core PCE (0.1% MoM vs 0.2% est) released July 30; BOJ held at 1% (8-1 vote), as expected, and USD/JPY recovered toward ~160 after the hold, with DXY trading near 99.90; July 30 close was ~100.98; 30-day change: June 30 ~101.34 → July 31 ~99.90 = -1.44%, clearly above the 0.5% relative flat threshold; trend down; status neutral (crossed below the 100.00 headwind threshold; supportive requires below 97.5).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 (10-year TIPS constant-maturity real yield) at 2.41% as of July 29, 2026 (FRED API proxy-blocked; value sourced from MacroRadar/CNBC US10YTIP cross-reference); soft Q2 GDP (1.5%) and core PCE (0.1% MoM) released July 30 may exert downward pressure on the July 31 DFII10 read (not yet published at run time); 4-week trend up: DFII10 rose from ~2.18% on June 30 to 2.41% on July 29 (+23bps, well above the 5bps flat threshold); status headwind (above 2% and rising on 4-week basis; September FOMC pivot is the primary near-term real-yield compression catalyst).

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: July 30, 2026 H.15 data: 10-year Treasury ~4.68–4.70% (held after July 29 FOMC +7bps move), 2-year Treasury ~4.236% (post-FOMC July 29, -4bps from prior); spread: 4.70% − 4.236% = +0.464% ≈ +0.44%; on July 31, BOJ intervention and soft macro data (Q2 GDP 1.5%, PCE 0.1% MoM) may push 10Y lower while 2Y holds near the Fed funds anchor; 4-week trend flat: spread moved from ~+0.40% (June 30) to +0.44% = +4bps, just below the 5bps steepening threshold; status neutral (positive spread, 4-week change below steepening threshold; not deeply inverted).

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL at $6.75T for week ending July 22, 2026 (H.4.1 released July 23): $4,516B Treasuries + $1,945B MBS + $287B other = $6,748B total; H.4.1 for week ending July 29, 2026 scheduled for release today (July 31) at 4:30 PM ET—value not yet available at run time; 4-week trend flat: balance sheet moved from ~$6.72T (week ending June 24) to $6.75T (+$0.03T = +0.45%), within the <0.5% relative flat threshold; status supportive (flat to marginally growing; QT effectively paused; no aggressive runoff with rising overnight rates).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: CoinGlass returned HTTP 403 again this run; value carried forward at +0.004%/8h (annualized ~+4.4%)—well below the 0.04%/8h overheating threshold; BTC price at $64,256 on July 31 (up slightly from $63,888 on July 30), consistent with a low-leverage spot-led market; BOJ hold (as expected) and continued DXY weakness did not trigger a significant funding spike; 30-day trend down (from ~+0.006%/8h in late June); status supportive (near-zero funding far from overheating).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$303B (USDT ~$184B, USDC ~$74.89B per SolCard/CoinLaw late-July 2026 data); total crypto market cap $2.27T (BTC $1.29T, BTC.D 56.55%); dominance: $303B / $2.27T = 13.35% ≈ 13.4%; 30-day trend down: TOTAL grew from ~$2.1T (June 30) to ~$2.27T (+8.1%) while stablecoin MC contracted from ~$315B to ~$303B, compressing dominance from ~15.0% to 13.4%—capital rotated from stablecoins into risk assets on 30-day basis; status supportive (falling 30-day basis; TOTAL up significantly over 30 days while stablecoins contracted).

upcoming.title: BOE Rate Decision (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Bank of England MPC decision at 12:00 BST (7:00 AM ET) alongside August 2026 Monetary Policy Report—current policy rate 3.75%; decision arrives one day after the BOJ held at 1.0% and amid soft global macro data (US Q2 GDP 1.5% below 2.1% forecast, core PCE 0.1% MoM); MPC vote split will be watched for dissenting views on cuts or hikes; the BoE's UK inflation trajectory and domestic economic resilience are the key inputs for the market's September central bank pivot assessment.

upcoming.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI (July 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM Manufacturing PMI for July 2026 at 10:00 AM ET—first Q3 manufacturing activity read and first major US macro print of August; prior June reading: 53.3% (sixth consecutive expansion month, -0.7pp from May's 54.0%); S&P Global US Manufacturing flash PMI for July edged down to 53.8 from 53.9, offering a cautious advance signal; markets will watch whether new orders (June: 56.0%) hold momentum and prices paid (June: 73.0%) continue moderating; a print above 54 with declining prices paid would reinforce the soft-landing thesis and the BTC Accumulation phase.

upcoming.title: JOLTS Job Openings (June 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey for June 2026 at 10:00 AM ET—key labor demand gauge arriving one day after the August 3 ISM Manufacturing print and two days before the July NFP; the FOMC's hawkish July 29-30 dissent (9-3 hold, 3 voters for a hike) means labor-softening signals carry elevated market impact through August; a reading below 7.5 million openings would reinforce the soft-landing thesis and add to the case for a September rate pause.

upcoming.title: ISM Services PMI (July 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM Services PMI for July 2026 at 10:00 AM ET—companion to the August 3 Manufacturing print; prior June 2026 reading: 54.0% (24th consecutive expansion month, -0.5pp from May's 54.5%), employment 51.2%, prices 67.7%; July reading is the second Q3 services data point framing September FOMC rate expectations; a reading above 54 with continued price moderation would reinforce the September pause case and weigh on DXY (currently near 99.90).

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended August 2, 2026)
upcoming.note: Weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET—the weekly labor market pulse released one day ahead of the July NFP (August 7); a print near or above 260k would reinforce soft labor market signals and add to the September rate pause case; the hawkish July 29-30 FOMC split (3 dissenters for a hike) keeps claims data elevated in market significance through August.

upcoming.title: Employment Situation / NFP (July 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Employment Situation for July 2026 at 8:30 AM ET—nonfarm payrolls, unemployment rate, and average hourly earnings; the primary labor market read ahead of the September FOMC; macro context: soft Q2 GDP (1.5% vs 2.1% est), soft core PCE (0.1% MoM), and BOJ holding at 1.0% all frame the risk backdrop; a weak NFP would open the door to a September cut discussion, further pressuring real yields (2.41%) and extending DXY's decline; a strong print with the current hawkish FOMC dissent would complicate the narrative and cap the crypto risk rally.
